answer: Validators lock collateral C and suffer quadratic slashing S = a*C^2 per equivocation, turning any Sybil set into a capital drain. A zero-knowledge verifiable delay forces each proposal to spend deterministic time t, so marginal attack cost grows as O(k*C^2*t) for k identities and exceeds any reward R. Since expected utility U = R - marginal_cost stays negative for all k>=1, the unique Nash equilibrium is honest behavior, making the network a secure haven where an ember of malice cannot sustain a pulse of fraud.
